html:
The Teke are a people of the plateaus north of Malebo Pool on the Congo River, in what are now the Republic of the Congo, Gabon and the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Their old kingdom, called Tio or Anziku, appears in Portuguese reports from the 1500s as a rival of Kongo. The map shows Teke land in 1880 and 1900.

The Tio king, called the Makoko, controlled the river trade at the Pool, where goods passed between the coast and the vast river network upstream.

That position made the Pool a prize in the scramble for Africa. In 1880 the Makoko Iloo signed a treaty with the French explorer Pierre Savorgnan de Brazza, placing his land under French protection. The French post on the north bank became Brazzaville, while Stanley, working for Leopold II, founded Leopoldville, today's Kinshasa, on the south bank.
